Epitome

/ih-PIT-uh-mee/ - rhymes with anatomy · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Epitome means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality.

With his pressed apron and pocket watch, the stationmaster was the epitome of old-railway courtesy.

Worked Example

In the knife maker's workshop hang a hundred blades, but apprentices are marched past all of them to one plain chef's knife on a black peg. Nothing about it shouts: the handle is unadorned, the steel unpolished past what work requires. Yet balance, edge, and temper meet in it so completely that the master simply calls it the lesson.

Epitome is the exact word for that knife, because epitome means a perfect example or embodiment of a quality — the whole idea of the craft, compressed into one object. Any blade on the wall is an example; the epitome is the example the others are judged against, the case that shows the quality at its purest.

How Epitome Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

embodiment

embodiment: the quality given a body — near-twin, minus the ranking against others

exemplar

exemplar: the model case held up for imitation

Antonyms

opposite

opposite: the quality reversed outright

mockery

mockery: a version so poor it insults the quality

How Strong Is It? — example → model → epitome

example vs. epitome

example vs. epitome: An example is any single case — it shows the quality without claiming to show it best.

model vs. epitome

model vs. epitome: A model stops short of the epitome — worth copying, yet still improvable; the epitome is the quality made flesh, with nothing left to add.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — epi-

Prefix — epi-: upon, on top

Root — tome

Root — tome: a cut, a slice (Greek temnein, to cut)

Put it together

Put it together: Epi- (upon) + tome (a cut) = a cutting-upon: Greek epitome was a work cut down to its essence, a summary. English kept the compression and moved it from books to qualities — today's epitome is a person or thing that holds the whole of a quality in one small, perfect cut.

Use the root in a new word: atom

Use the root in a new word: atom: A- means not, so the Greeks named the atom the thing that cannot be cut any smaller — the same tom- blade at work.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / appreciative

Epitome is praise with a superlative built in: call someone the epitome of patience and you rank them, not just describe them. Embodiment is the near-twin without the ranking; exemplar is cooler and more instructional. Paradigm, met among this unit's reference words, is different furniture — a pattern others follow, not a quality made flesh. And note the fixed frame: always the epitome OF something.
